overview: Arenas on demand. Pick a preset from a menu and a fresh piece of ground is made for the fight, floating alone in a dimension of its own, gone when the clock runs out.

1.8.3: Guess who's black and brown bears are Beets Bears' own animals, wearing their own coats again.
Arenas can't be joined from the Learning Blocks classroom: leave the classroom first, so your own things stay with you.
1.8.2: Cops and robbers, for two teams: the cops tag robbers into an iron-barred jail that any free robber can spring, while the robbers steal gold from the cops' vault and bank it in their hideout.
In Guess who, ringing your bell with one suspect left standing accuses it.

Guess who has many more suspects: zombies and skeletons (in leather caps against the sun), piglins, wardens, dolphins, camels and more, every baby as a suspect of its own, ores, Nether and End blocks, beacons and cakes, and items floating over their squares, from a diamond or a trident to water and lava in their buckets; and our other mods' blocks, items, bears and baby skeletons when those mods are on the server.
1.8.1: Battleship is played as at the table: a wall down the middle, and each side lays its own fleet by hand before the shooting starts.
Each team has two grids, its own fleet with the other side's shots landing on it, and their waters to fire at.
Pool balls bounce off the cushions instead of stopping dead, and can't get stuck in the rail.
Bowling pins are two cubes stacked: knock one and its head flies off.
Minesweeper points add up across fields: a mine costs you the field, not the squares you've cleared.
Connect four drops cubes in your colour down glass channels.
Hot potato sticks to whoever has it, over their head: hit somebody to pass it on.
Guess who's suspects are real mobs and blocks, drawn fresh each game, with a wall between the galleries.
Golf is played in turns, a shot each. Crouch to chip the ball up and over; a ball in water comes back a stroke the worse.
1.8.0: Bowling: a lane a team, ten pins, ten frames scored as at any alley.
Connect four, for two teams: drop pieces down a frame in the middle; first to three games.
Code breaking: every team races to crack a code of four colours, with black and white pegs for each try.
Memory: thirty-six cards in the middle, eighteen pairs, turned over two at a time.
Minesweeper: a field each, numbers on the ground, and the first team to clear theirs wins.
Balls now knock into each other in golf and soccer, and soccer can have up to three balls in play.
1.7.0: Guess who, for two teams: a gallery of sixteen suspects at each end. Ask a yes-or-no question out loud, flip down who it rules out, ring your bell; right-click your suspect twice to accuse.
1.6.0: Battleship, for two teams: hidden fleets, and a board at each end to fire from. Right-click a square on your turn; sink their whole fleet first.
1.5.0: Pool: a table, a rack in each team's colour and the 8-ball. Take turns at the white, crouch for a soft shot, clear your colour, then sink the 8.
1.4.2: Invite on the Arena menu picks who to bring in by face.
Join lists the arenas running to pick from, instead of putting you in the first one it finds.
1.4.1: Arena matches keep their own PvP rules whatever an op has trusted anyone with outside them.
1.1.0: The arena is a menu: arenas, join, loadout, begin and leave are buttons, not things you type.
A match ends on the score it was played for: banks filled, flags taken, the hill held.
It says so plainly when the clock runs out with nobody ahead.
A team's bank is counted even when nobody is standing near it.
Dying outside an arena puts you back in your own bed.
1.0.1: The odd one out: everybody but one is dealt the place, and the room finds who was not.
It ends in a scramble anybody can call.
A snowball fight, scored by what lands rather than by damage.
Players sit down while the talking is on.
A plain teleport into or out of an arena is refused, and says what the door does.
1.0.0: /pvp opens a menu of presets: a fresh arena inside a border, everyone invited by a button.
The empty obsidian frame beside you is lit as the way in.
Everybody is sent home when the time is up.
Admins make and edit presets; users start the ones marked for them.
